description: A single-panel process flow chart (no axes, no micrographs) laying out the laboratory-scale thermomechanical route for low-density sheet steels. It reads top-to-bottom down the left for the hot-rolling line and bottom-to-top up the right for the downstream finishing line. The left column runs "Ingot casting" → down arrow → "Reheating 1250 °C" → "Rough rolling" → a second "Reheating 1250 °C" → "Hot rolling" annotated "t_final = 3.5 mm" and "FRT 900 °C" → "Run-out table cooling". A right-pointing arrow leads to "Coiling", after which the path ascends: "Pickling 85 °C, HCl" → "Cold rolling, or Warm (250 °C) rolling" annotated "t_final = 1 mm" → "Continuous annealing 850-900 °C" → "Aging 400-700 °C". Two alloy labels, "Fe-Al-(C)" and "Fe-Al-Mn-C", sit beside the first descending arrow below Ingot casting; a third label, "Fe-Mn-Al-C", sits beside the arrow from Continuous annealing to Aging. All boxed steps, temperatures, the HCl pickling medium and the thickness targets are printed inside the boxes. The chart demonstrates that Fe-Al and Fe-Al-Mn-C low-density steels share one conventional ingot-casting/hot-rolling/cold-rolling/annealing route with no additional process step, the alloy-specific differences being the choice of cold versus warm rolling and whether the aging stage is applied.

observations.observation: The flow chart starts at a box labelled 'Ingot casting' and every step is connected to the next by a thick solid purple arrow.
The box 'Reheating 1250 °C' appears twice in the route: once before 'Rough rolling' and again before 'Hot rolling'.
The 'Hot rolling' box is annotated 't_final = 3.5 mm' and 'FRT 900 °C'.
After 'Run-out table cooling' a right-pointing arrow leads to an isolated 'Coiling' box, from which the process chain continues in the upward direction.
The rolling box reads 'Cold rolling, or Warm (250 °C) rolling' and is annotated 't_final = 1 mm'.
Two anneal/age steps are shown in sequence: 'Continuous annealing 850-900 °C' and 'Aging 400-700 °C'.
The alloy labels 'Fe-Al-(C)' and 'Fe-Al-Mn-C' are printed beside the first downward arrow, between 'Ingot casting' and 'Reheating 1250 °C'.
The alloy label 'Fe-Mn-Al-C' is printed beside the arrow leading from 'Continuous annealing 850-900 °C' up to 'Aging 400-700 °C'.
The figure is a flow chart of the typical processing steps applied to produce various Fe-Al and Fe-Al-Mn-C ferritic and multiphase sheet steels at the laboratory scale.
The citing text states that these processing steps correspond to industrial production routes used for conventional automotive steels, with no additional process step involved.

The citing text states that the thermomechanical parameters in this route (e.g. temperature, cooling rate, rolling reduction) depend on the alloy chemistry and desired microstructure; these values are not printed in the flow chart.

The citing text gives coiling temperatures of 650 °C for ultralow-C/interstitial-free Fe-Al-(C) alloys, 400 °C for lean Fe-Mn-Al-C steels and room-temperature coiling for rich Fe-Mn-Al-C steels; the flow chart's 'Coiling' box carries no temperature.

The citing text reports that a cold-rolling thickness reduction of 66.67% can be applied to multiphase Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys, and that warm rolling is used for ferritic grades with Al content greater than 8 wt.% because higher-Al alloys crack during cold rolling.

subfigures.description: Single flow chart panel: boxed processing steps linked by thick purple arrows. Downward chain on the left: Ingot casting, Reheating 1250 °C, Rough rolling, Reheating 1250 °C, Hot rolling (t_final = 3.5 mm, FRT 900 °C), Run-out table cooling. A right arrow goes to Coiling, then the chain climbs upward on the right: Pickling 85 °C, HCl; Cold rolling, or Warm (250 °C) rolling (t_final = 1 mm); Continuous annealing 850-900 °C; Aging 400-700 °C. Alloy annotations: Fe-Al-(C) and Fe-Al-Mn-C near the first down arrow, Fe-Mn-Al-C beside the arrow from continuous annealing to aging.
